findings.title: Published checkpoint evidence names a non-transportable input
findings.originalExpected: A canonical checkpoint tag must validate from a fresh remote transport clone without depending on repository metadata, ignored output or producer-local temporary files.
findings.originalObserved: GATE-4-CP-0006 validated locally but failed from its published canonical tag because COMMANDS.jsonl cmd-0061 declared .git/gate4-cp0006-pre-red-retry.zip as an input.
findings.rootCause: The recorder and validator delegated generated-input classification to git check-ignore, which does not classify Git's own metadata namespace. Validation also accepted local presence before transportability, and explicit or directly constructed input lists could bypass auto-detection.
implementation: Checkpoint schema 3.3.0 adds a forward-only invariant that every declared command input is eligible for Git transport.
One shared classifier rejects Git metadata, ignored output, absolute paths and repository escapes for auto-detection, explicit inputs and checkpoint validation.
The recorder rejects an explicit local-only input before execution and records the refused attempt with a dedicated result code.
Schemas through 3.2.0 retain digest-bound compatibility for immutable generated inputs, so current tooling can audit sealed predecessors without rewriting them.
The corrective checkpoint carries validation reports and digests while generated review ZIPs remain outputs outside the input set.
negativeTest: cmd-0005 preserves the original remote-clone failure under CP0006's tag-carried validator.
cmd-0010 records the expected E_NONTRANSPORT_INPUT refusal for an explicit .git/HEAD input before the child command starts.
CP0006 and its canonical tag remain unchanged.
